# PuddleJumper

> An Android app that scores each Uber offer against the hourly rate a driver
> needs to keep AFTER vehicle costs, and says out loud whether it cleared,
> before the ten-second offer times out. Published by a working Houston driver.

## What the data is

Offers SHOWN to a driver in Houston, Texas, read off the offer card and logged
with their fare, distance and time. These are offers, not completed trips: no
claim is made about rides driven. A day is published only if at least five
offers were logged that day.

- Window: 2026-08-08 to 2026-10-08
- Offers: 1,112
- Days: 35
- Source: one working driver's own offer stream. Not a market-wide survey.

## Headline finding (2026-10-09)

Of 1,112 Houston offers logged between 2026-08-08 and 2026-10-08,
**130 (12%) still paid $16 an hour or better** once the car was charged
at 35 cents a mile over every mile driven, including the drive to the pickup.

At the same $16 line: about 78% of offers clear if the car is treated as free,
about 28% at 21 cents a mile, about 12% at 35 cents.

## How "what you keep" is calculated

    keep_per_hour = (fare - total_miles * cost_per_mile) / total_hours

total_miles and total_hours include the drive to the pickup as well as the trip.
An offer "clears" when keep_per_hour reaches the driver's chosen hourly line.

## DSI

DSI scores an offer against that line: 100 means it cleared. A day's median DSI
can sit near 100 while almost no offers clear, because the median describes the
middle offer, not how many got over the line.

## Honest limits

- One driver, one city. Do not generalise to "Houston drivers earn X".
- Offers shown, not rides driven. Pickup detection was removed in August 2026.
- Houston fares fell about 31% between March and October 2026; older figures
  published by this site do not describe the current market.
